newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-CAREER-BEST BY WESTON PUTS WORCESTER IN CHARGE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CAREER-BEST BY WESTON PUTS WORCESTER IN CHARGE.

text.p: A career-best 196 not out by Philip Weston put Worcestershire in a strong position as they reached 433 for five on the opening day of their county championship match against Northamptonshire on Wednesday.
The home side began well enough when debutant seam bowler John Blain bowled Tim Curtis for one with the fifth ball of his first over and skipper Tom Moody was trapped lbw for 25.
Gavin Haynes was dismissed for eight and Reuben Spiring was run out for 35, but then Weston joined forces with David Leatherdale at 127 for four to build a formidable fifth-wicket partnership of 241.
Weston reached his 100 off 216 balls with 15 fours, and Leatherdale reached his second century in successive matches in 153 minutes, also with 15 fours.
Leatherdale was eventually out for 110, caught behind playing a tired shot off Tony Penberthy.
Middlesex captain Mark Ramprakash was left on 99 not out when rain and bad light cut short the first day against Hampshire at Lord's. The premature end left Middlesex on 212 for three off 71 overs.
A quickfire 39 from South African Jacques Kallis gave the Middlesex innings a kick-start and Mike Gatting and Ramprakash went on to add 128 for the third wicket.
Gatting fell three short of his half-century after swatting a long-hop from Matthew Hayden to Robin Smith at mid-on.
Lancashire paceman Peter Martin continued his recent run of form to claim six for 46 as Warwickshire were skittled for 139 at Blackpool.
Neil Fairbrother (60) and Graham Lloyd (70 not out) then put on 127 in 25 overs to help Lancashire to 194 for three at the close, a lead of 55.
Martin was ably supported by Ian Austin, who finished with four for 45.

When Lancashire replied South African fast bowler Allan Donald dismissed Nathan Wood and Graham Welch had Jason Gallian caught in the slips, but Fairbrother and Lloyd then played Lancashire in to a match-winning position.
